criterion.purpose: one pre-registered intervention on top of round22: add a training-only privileged auxiliary task - predict which screen half holds the safe gap from the GRU state - so that the objective, not just the representation, has to use the position round22 proved is linearly decodable at 98.5%, and read the result out mechanistically

intervention.change: a Linear(256,2) auxiliary head on the GRU state, plus an auxiliary cross-entropy term in the training loss with a fixed weight
intervention.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap's screen-x centre lies left or right of x=192; label = round21.telegraph_gap(s), i.e. s.gap under s.mirror

label.source: s.gap under s.mirror through round21.telegraph_gap, i.e. exactly the arithmetic the R21 renderer uses to draw the band
label.availability: training only; never an input, never a history field, never a pixel region, never a tensor of the policy head

supervision.window: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
supervision.why: outside the telegraph window the band is not drawn yet, so the label would ask the head to guess rather than to read; F2/F3 worlds have `internal_gap = False` and therefore no label at all
supervision.labelled_events: the six F1 train events (3 groups x base/mirror)
supervision.unlabelled_events: the eight F2/F3 train events contribute an exactly-zero auxiliary term

head.placement: outside `heads`, so the policy head state dict, its SHA and the whole checkpoint contract are unchanged from round22

intervention.loss: L = L_control + w * CE(aux_logits, side);  w = 0.0 for arm A, 0.5 for arm X
intervention.gradient_path: the auxiliary term reaches only the auxiliary head and the shared GRU; the residual head, the option/target/urgency/termination/slack heads and the frozen backbone are untouched by it
intervention.head_class: no line of TacticalPolicy is overridden: the auxiliary head is downstream of the GRU, so the parent detach of `features` is inert for it (contrast round22, whose upstream fusion layer required the detach to be removed)
intervention.state_source: forward pre-hook on heads["option"]; the unit tests recompute all five heads that consume it from the captured tensor and assert bitwise equality
intervention.not_changed: worlds, world parameters, R19 split, round21 renderer and pixels, teacher actions, tactical labels, pixel packing, encoder, control loss, optimizer, learning rate, clip value, clip scope (the policy head in both arms), sequence, batch, update count, seed set, closed-loop runner, condition, masking
intervention.parameter_increment: X and A are identical objects: 429200 policy-head parameters + 514 auxiliary parameters = 429714 active; the arms differ only in w

data.source: round21 run/records.json assets, reopened read-only and SHA-bound per event; nothing re-rendered, no teacher called, no tactical label created
data.features: round22.spatial_vectors reused verbatim; its spatial digest must recompute to round22's frozen 83a75f73... so "the head sees round22's features" is a measured identity, not a copy

train.use: the only events encoded or trained on

validation.use: read-only: never trained, never labelled for training, never encoded into the training set; closed loop and diagnostic probes only. The auxiliary probe re-renders each checkpoint's own stored trajectory and uses the label only to score it

data.bindings: pixels.npz, history.pt, labels.pt and rollout.json must equal round21's frozen SHA table for all 14 train events, otherwise the run aborts

arms.A: the same auxiliary head with weight 0.0: the round22 control
arms.X: the same auxiliary head with weight 0.5

training.clip_scope: the 429200 policy-head parameters, identically in both arms; the auxiliary head is outside the clip so that the clipping rule covers the same tensor set in both arms and the control's floating-point path stays round22's
training.precision: FP32 without AMP, autocast disabled, matmul TF32 False, cuDNN TF32 False, float32 matmul precision highest
training.loop: round20 train_all with three additions only: the auxiliary term, its weight and the saved auxiliary state
training.initialization: fresh seed reset per construction; the head is built first, so the policy head SHA must equal the frozen R16/R20/R21/R22 table for the seed; the auxiliary head is built afterwards from the same RNG state in both arms, so its SHA must be identical in both arms
training.control_reproduction: arm A must reproduce round22's A checkpoint and its closed-loop rows bitwise; if it does not, that is reported as `control_not_reproduced` and the causal claim is withheld
training.selection: final step only: no early stopping, no validation-based selection, no tuning of lr/clip/weight/epochs/order; the auxiliary weight is fixed at 0.5 before the run

evaluation.order: all six checkpoints written and SHA-frozen first; then the six R18 baselines, then B0, then the six checkpoints, validation before train; then the probes
evaluation.executor: round21.run_event_rendered / round21.closed_loop reused verbatim, so the evaluation code is round21 code and not a copy; the network is a plain TacticalPolicy, so the auxiliary head has no path into the closed loop
evaluation.b0: the frozen baseline policy logits on the identical telegraph renders; a reference, not a capability
evaluation.six_baselines: round20.six_baselines re-executed on the same worlds; the 168 rows must equal round22's
evaluation.holdout_rule: if ANY of the six R18 baselines is feasible on ANY validation event the R18 filter has failed on the holdout side: report it verbatim and withhold the learning conclusion

definitions.direction: rebuild the logical-frame x trace from the executed actions with `advance` semantics (round21.gap_trace), take the canonical displacement start -> wall_frame-1: that is `direction`; `screen_direction` is the same displacement in raw x
definitions.toward: the canonical direction points from the start's canonical x at the gap's canonical centre, so `toward` is "moved toward the slot" regardless of the mirror; `away` is the opposite and `hold` is zero net motion
definitions.parked: `signed_error_px` is measured at wall_frame-1 in canonical px: 0 inside [gap0, gap1], negative short of the left edge, positive past the right edge
definitions.mirror_flip_rate: the fraction of mirror-group cells whose canonical motion is toward the gap; because the same screen-right prior is right in the base group and wrong in the mirror group, this is the direction flip this round is about
definitions.identical_cells: for every seed, the number of the 14 validation events on which the two arms have the same first-hit frame
definitions.toward_but_late: a cell whose verdict is `toward` and whose entered_gap is False: it moved the right way and still never reached the slot before the wall
definitions.aux_accuracy: the auxiliary head on the preview-window rows of the six F1 validation events, replayed along each checkpoint's own stored trajectory; the label scores the prediction and is never an input; chance is 0.5 because the six labels are balanced 3/3 on both splits

primary_metrics: F1 holdout, per group (base / mirror) and per arm: cells that move toward the gap, hold, or move away, plus the mirror toward rate (the direction flip this round is about)

F1 holdout, per cell: whether the x at wall_frame-1 is inside the gap, the signed parking error in px, whether the cell moved toward the gap but never reached it before the wall, and the frame of first movement
per family F1/F2/F3 and pooled: feasible and survived per network, every event first hit, totals, and for each seed the number of validation events whose first hit is identical between the arms
the auxiliary head's accuracy, balanced accuracy and 2x2 confusion on the held-out geometry (and on the seen training rows as fit), per arm, per seed, per event

the "learned but unused" read-out: per cell, the auxiliary side read, its correctness, the policy's screen direction, the verdict and the parking error side by side; plus the ridge decodability of the same side from the GRU state, arm A against arm X

probe_caveats.aux_accuracy: the label is balanced 3/3 on both splits, so chance is 0.5 and a majority baseline cannot beat it; but the label is constant within an event, so an event-level read-out is the honest unit and the per-row accuracy is only a summary of it
probe_caveats.label_leakage: the label is a function of exactly the geometry the renderer draws, so the auxiliary task adds no information that is not in the pixels - it adds a target. What is privileged is the label, not the content
probe_caveats.decodability: 132 rows against 256 dimensions with a label constant within an event: the probe separates events as much as frames, so only the whole lambda sweep and the arm-to-arm comparison are read
probe_caveats.replay: the replay re-renders each checkpoint's own x trace; its fidelity (the stored masked argmax reproduced step by step) is reported for every cell

evaluation.reporting: per family, never only aggregated; n=3 seeds; F2 validation has one group; mirrors are not independent samples; every F1 cell is listed
evaluation.degeneracy: single_candidate and switches<=1 are counted, listed and reported, never dropped silently

verdict_rules.equivalence: arm A must reproduce round22's A checkpoint SHA and every closed-loop row bitwise; if it does not, the round reports `control_not_reproduced` and withholds the causal claim
verdict_rules.improvement: F1 validation feasible per seed, X minus A: any seed strictly greater = improved, all equal = unchanged, any seed lower = worse
verdict_rules.mechanism: the mirror toward rate, the parking errors and the auxiliary accuracies are reported as counts, px and rates, never as a significance claim
verdict_rules.honesty: if the mirror direction does not improve while the auxiliary head is accurate, the round must report the "the task was learned, the policy did not use it" reading with its cell-level evidence; if the mirror direction flips but the cells die on timing, the round must report the flip and the timing failure together; neither may be left implicit
verdict_rules.aux_learned: the auxiliary task counts as learned on the holdout only if the balanced accuracy exceeds 0.5 and the event-level read is correct on the same side of chance for all three seeds; a single seed above chance is reported as one seed, not as learned

claims.significance: none: 3 seeds, 7 validation groups, at most 14 independent geometries; descriptive only
claims.gate: no formal gate opened, no deployable checkpoint produced, no game executed
claims.can_show: whether a fixed-weight privileged auxiliary task on the shared GRU state makes the same N1 head stop being dominated by the screen-right prior, and if not, whether the auxiliary task was learned at all
claims.cannot_show: tactical understanding, learnability beyond these 7 held-out geometries, or that a privileged label at training time is a legitimate route to a deployable policy

criterion.failure_policy: first failure retained; one run; no retrain, rerun, repair of numbers, extra epoch, tuning or baseline switch

split.rule: one group = base + mirror, atomic; within each family the groups are ordered by group name (candidate index) and alternate train/validation starting with train at index 0; the two F2 groups therefore give one train and one validation group

auxiliary.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap's screen-x centre lies left or right of x=192; label = round21.telegraph_gap(s), i.e. s.gap under s.mirror
auxiliary.supervision_window: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
auxiliary.head: Linear(256, 2, bias=True) outside `heads`
auxiliary.parent_detach: inert: the auxiliary head is downstream of the GRU, so no line of the parent body is overridden
auxiliary.inference: the closed loop builds a plain TacticalPolicy from payload["heads"]; the auxiliary state is never loaded and there is no module to hold it

features.note: the 94-d spatial vector that function also returns is not used; it is the frozen proof that the encode pass is round22's

initialization.method: fresh seed reset immediately before every N1 construction after the backbone load, through the frozen r16 recipe; the auxiliary head is constructed afterwards, so it cannot move the head initialisation and both arms are byte-identical objects at step 0

round22_reference.decodability: round22 probe: 256-d trunk features 0.985 side accuracy on the held-out geometry (lambda sweep 0.953-0.985); the 94-d pooled vector 0.674
round22_reference.behaviour: round22: 95-97% of telegraph-window decisions are hold; every F1 death is on wall_frame; the fusion delta is 94.4% constant

prerequisites: every training asset equals round21's frozen SHA
the round22 spatial digest recomputes to 83a75f73...
the round22 feature-norm table recomputes exactly
the initial head SHA equals the frozen table for every seed
the initial auxiliary SHA equals the pre-registration for every seed and is identical in both arms
the six R18 baselines reproduce round22's 168 rows
verification.control: arm A must equal round22's A checkpoint SHA and its closed-loop rows for all 3 seeds; otherwise it is reported as `control_not_reproduced` and the causal claim is withheld
verification.step0: a unit test asserts that step 0 of arm X is bitwise arm A (identical policy logits, identical masked action) and that perturbing the auxiliary parameters changes no policy logit

failure_policy: first failure retained; one run; no retrain, rerun, repair, overwrite, extra epoch or baseline switch
